title: [ci] Six more jobs declare no `timeout-minutes` — the uncached half of the surface objectui#7270 bounded
body:
Found while implementing objectui#7270, as an out-of-scope finding. Recording it rather than acting on it: objectui#7270 scoped itself to the three **cached** jobs and its dispatch pinned the file surface to those three workflows, so these six were deliberately not touched there.

Attribution as prose: generated by Claude Code, dev session `session_013uAaxiwgYDybsTNV9xwa1M`, while implementing objectui#7270.

## The observation

Measured by parsing every workflow file on `3b30920f1` (control: 34 files enumerated, 42 jobs parsed, non-zero). objectui#7270 bounded three of the nine jobs that declared no job-level `timeout-minutes`. These six still declare none, so their ceiling is GitHub's documented default of **360 minutes**:

| workflow | job |
|:--|:--|
| `changelog.yml` | `changelog` |
| `changeset-release.yml` | `lane` |
| `check-links.yml` | `check-links` |
| `cross-repo-issue-closer.yml` | `close-foreign-issues` |
| `labeler.yml` | `label` |
| `stale.yml` | `stale` |

## Why objectui#7270 stopped where it did — the selector was real, not an oversight

Its title says *cached* jobs, and that selector holds under measurement: none of these six uses `actions/cache` in any form, and none passes `cache:` to `actions/setup-node`. They are marketplace-action jobs. So the specific hazard objectui#7270 was written around — a runner-generated cache-save post step that no workflow syntax can bound — is absent here. What remains is the generic exposure: any step in them is backstopped by nothing but 360.

⚠️ One of the six is worth naming on its own: `changeset-release.yml` now has `lane` unbounded sitting directly above `release` bounded at 40. Two jobs, one file, two answers.

## ⛔ What this does NOT claim

- ⛔ **No hang has been observed in any of these six.** This is exposure, not a defect.
- ⛔ Not a claim that 360 is wrong for them. objectui#7270's own constraint applies unchanged: a ceiling set below a job's honest slowest run converts a working gate into a permanently red one, so any number has to be derived per job from that job's own measured distribution, never inherited.
- ⛔ **Not verified here which, if any, of these six produce required contexts.** objectui#7270's stakes argument leaned on two of its three being required on a shared serial queue; that argument has not been re-run for these, and re-running it is part of triage rather than a thing this card asserts.

## What triage decides

The same one decision objectui#7270 faced, on a cheaper surface: accept 360 for these six and record that choice in the workflows, or derive a ceiling per job. The recipe for the second option is now written down in three places — the derivation comments objectui#7270 left beside `lint.yml::lint`, `performance-budget.yml::bundle-analysis` and `changeset-release.yml::release` state the window, the sample size, the min/median/p95/max and the rule, and the pin in `scripts/__tests__/workflow-cache-save-bound.test.ts` is where any new ceiling would be held.

Refs: objectui#7270, objectui#7048, objectui#6577, objectui#5304
